chapter.name: Salient Features of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: Size, amendment methods, parliamentary and federal features, the Parts and Schedules, and the sources from which the Constitution borrowed.

scope_in.item: Salient features: size, amendment modes, federal and parliamentary features, judiciary, citizenship, franchise, emergencies
Parts of the Constitution (I to XXII) and Schedules (First to Twelfth)
Sources of the Constitution and the federal-yet-unitary summary

scope_out.item: Features of the Constitution not in these notes (secularism, independent bodies, three-tier government) beyond the Laxmikanth additions
scope_out.reason: not part of the notes pages; covered by the Laxmikanth packs lk04/lk04b

scope_out.item: Five-Year Plans as a USSR borrowing
scope_out.reason: not a constitutional feature and not in Laxmikanth Table 4.4

concepts.name: Size, amendment methods and basic features
concepts.description: How long the Constitution is, how it can be amended (simple majority, special majority, special majority with ratification), the Union of States, the parliamentary system, an integrated and independent judiciary, single citizenship and adult franchise.
concepts.idea: The Constitution is long and detailed, blends rigidity and flexibility, and is federal with a unitary bias.
concepts.rule: At adoption the Constitution had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; it now has 25 Parts and 12 Schedules (Laxmikanth: about 470 Articles). Some provisions are amended by a simple majority outside Article 368; most need a special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting and a majority of total membership of each House); federal matters need in addition ratification by half the States. Article 1 calls India a Union of States, so the federation is not the result of an agreement and no State can secede. The system is parliamentary with a dual executive, collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha and ministers from Parliament; the judiciary is integrated and independent, citizenship is single, and the voting age is 18 (61st Amendment, 1988).
concepts.example: A bill changing the quorum of Parliament needs only a simple majority, but a bill changing the representation of States in Parliament needs a special majority and ratification by half the States.

questions.q: Under the amendment scheme of the Constitution, which one of the following matters cannot be changed without the ratification of at least half of the States, in addition to a special majority in each House of Parliament?
questions.a: Legislative powers as divided between the Union and the States
o: Legislative powers as divided between the Union and the States
The quorum required for the sittings of the Houses of Parliament
Salaries, allowances and privileges of the Members of Parliament
The provisions governing the official language of the Union
questions.e: Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States affects the federal structure, so it needs a special majority plus ratification by half of the States. The other three are simple-majority subjects outside Article 368 (also in Laxmikanth ch.4 pp.63-64 on the three modes of amendment).
w: Quorum is changeable by a simple majority, outside Article 368.
Salaries and privileges are in the simple-majority group, with no ratification.
Official-language provisions are listed among the simple-majority subjects.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the 'special majority' with which most provisions of the Constitution may be amended under Article 368?
questions.a: Two-thirds of those present and voting plus a majority of the full House, in each House
o: Two-thirds of those present and voting plus a majority of the full House, in each House
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House, and a majority of the members present and voting
A majority of the total membership of each House sitting together in a joint session, and no separate vote
Two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Lok Sabha, with the Rajya Sabha only able to delay the Bill
questions.e: Special majority = two-thirds of members present and voting AND a majority of total membership of each House (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.63).
w: Reverses the two thresholds: the two-thirds is of members present and voting; the majority is of total membership.
The Constitution provides no joint sitting for amendments; each House must pass the Bill separately.
The Rajya Sabha has an equal voice in a constitutional amendment; it has no merely delaying role.

questions.q: India's founders chose to call the country a 'Union of States' in Article 1 rather than use the word 'federation'. Which one of the following does this expression imply?
questions.a: The federation did not arise from an agreement among the States, and no State has a right to secede
o: The federation did not arise from an agreement among the States, and no State has a right to secede
The federation arose from an agreement among the States, but no State can secede from it
The federation did not arise from an agreement among the States, but a State may secede by a special majority of Parliament
The federation arose from an agreement among the States, which therefore keep a right to leave it
questions.e: Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States', which implies that the federation is not the result of an agreement among states and that no state has the right to secede; the word 'federation' itself appears nowhere in the Constitution (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.64).
w: Wrong on the origin: the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the States.
No State has any right of secession; Parliament's power is over boundaries, not exit.
Both halves are wrong: no agreement, and no right to secede.

questions.q: Since the Constitution came into force, four Parts were added and one Part was deleted, and Schedules numbered Ninth to Twelfth were added. Which one of the following gives the resulting present structure?
questions.a: 25 Parts and 12 Schedules, against 22 Parts and 8 Schedules at adoption
o: 25 Parts and 12 Schedules, against 22 Parts and 8 Schedules at adoption
26 Parts and 12 Schedules, against 22 Parts and 8 Schedules at adoption
25 Parts and 10 Schedules, against 22 Parts and 8 Schedules at adoption
22 Parts and 12 Schedules, against 22 Parts and 8 Schedules at adoption
questions.e: Original text: 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. Parts IV-A, IX-A, IX-B and XIV-A were added and Part VII deleted: 22 + 4 - 1 = 25; Schedules Ninth to Twelfth were added: 8 + 4 = 12 (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.62).
w: Counts 22 + 4 and forgets that Part VII was deleted: 22 + 4 - 1 = 25.
Four Schedules (Ninth to Twelfth) were added, so 8 + 4 = 12, not 10.
The Parts did change: IV-A, IX-A, IX-B and XIV-A were added and VII deleted, giving 25.
tr: arithmetic with an addition and a deletion

questions.q: The age of voting in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years. Which one of the following correctly identifies the amending Act and the year from which the lowered age applied?
questions.a: 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988, operative from 1989
o: 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988, operative from 1989
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, operative from 1977
44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978, operative from 1979
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992, operative from 1993
questions.e: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years in 1989 by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.68).
w: The 42nd Amendment inserted Fundamental Duties and 'secular' in the Preamble; it did not change the voting age.
The 44th Amendment removed the right to property from Part III; the voting age was untouched.
The 73rd Amendment added Part IX on Panchayats, not a change in the voting age.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the comparative size of constitutions, with the figures given in the text and the footnote of Laxmikanth:

1. The United States Constitution originally consisted of only seven Articles.
2. The Australian Constitution contains 138 Articles.
3. According to the Laxmikanth footnote, the Canadian Constitution has 147 Articles.
4. The Indian text is very long partly because it had to accommodate many languages, religions, castes, tribal groups and regional identities.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the US text is the shortest of the comparison, at seven Articles. Statement 2 is incorrect: Australia has 128 Articles; 138 is the figure Laxmikanth gives for China. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.83 footnote 2 gives 147 for Canada. Statement 4 is correct: diversity is the reason given for the large size.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.83
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.83
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.83

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the size and growth of the Indian Constitution:

1. As adopted, the Constitution had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 9 Schedules.
2. According to Laxmikanth, the Constitution at present has about 470 Articles divided into 25 Parts.
3. India has the lengthiest written Constitution among the countries of the world.
4. The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, made provision for the reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it had 8 Schedules at adoption; the Ninth to Twelfth came later. Statement 2 is correct: the chapter gives about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules (ch.4 p.62). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth describes it as the lengthiest written Constitution in the world. Statement 4 is correct: the 106th Amendment (2023) is the women's reservation amendment, the latest numbered amendment in the count used here.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.62
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about amendments carried out by a simple majority of Parliament:

1. The formation of new States can be provided for by Parliament by a simple majority.
2. Laws on the election of Parliament and of the State legislatures may be changed by a simple majority.
3. Amendments to the Fundamental Rights can be made by a simple majority, outside Article 368.
4. Amendments to the Directive Principles of State Policy can be made by a simple majority, outside Article 368.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: formation of new states is a simple-majority subject. Statement 2 is correct: election of Parliament and State legislatures is a simple-majority subject. Statement 3 is incorrect: Fundamental Rights are amended by the special-majority route under Article 368. Statement 4 is incorrect: Directive Principles are likewise amended by special majority under Article 368.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rigid part of the amending scheme:

1. Fundamental Rights are amended through the special-majority route of Article 368.
2. Directive Principles of State Policy can be amended by a simple majority outside Article 368.
3. Provisions not placed in the simple-majority or the ratification categories are amended by the special-majority route.
4. A special majority means two-thirds of the total membership of each House of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: crucial provisions need special majority. Statement 2 is incorrect: Directive Principles are amended by special majority. Statement 3 is correct: special majority is the residual route. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is two-thirds of the members present and voting, plus a majority of the total membership.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following matters in the context of amendments that require, besides a special majority, ratification by half of the States:

1. Election of the President.
2. Representation of the States in Parliament.
3. Salaries and privileges of the Members of Parliament.
4. The amendment procedure contained in Article 368 itself.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: election of the President needs ratification by half the States. Statement 2 is correct: representation of States in Parliament needs ratification. Statement 3 is incorrect: this is a simple-majority subject, outside Article 368. Statement 4 is correct: Article 368 itself can be changed only with ratification by half the States.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the parliamentary form of government in India:

1. The President is the nominal head, while the Prime Minister with the Council of Ministers is the real executive.
2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha and must resign if it loses majority support there.
3. A person who is not a Member of Parliament can remain a minister for a year before becoming one.
4. The Lok Sabha is dissolved by the President acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: dual executive. Statement 2 is incorrect: collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is incorrect: the limit is six months. Statement 4 is correct: dissolution is on the PM's advice in practice; the Council led by the PM advises the President.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judiciary, citizenship and the franchise in India:

1. The Supreme Court, the High Courts and the subordinate courts form a single unified hierarchy.
2. Judicial independence implies that the judiciary decides cases free from the control of the legislature and the executive.
3. India has a single citizenship, unlike the United States, where a person is a citizen both of the Union and of a State.
4. Under universal adult franchise, citizens aged 18 or above may vote without discrimination of caste, gender, religion or economic status.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: integrated judiciary. Statement 2 is correct: independence of the judiciary from legislative and executive control. Statement 3 is correct: single citizenship contrasted with the USA. Statement 4 is correct: universal adult franchise, subject to the usual statutory disqualifications.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.13
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.13
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.13

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In Article 1 the country is named a 'Federal Union of States'.
2. The word 'federation' is nowhere used in the Constitution.
3. The right to vote at 18 depends on a minimum level of literacy or property.
4. The 61st Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years, and the change operated from 1989.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 1 says 'Union of States', not 'Federal Union'. Statement 2 is correct: also in Laxmikanth ch.4 p.64. Statement 3 is incorrect: adult franchise is irrespective of caste, gender, religion or economic status. Statement 4 is correct: the 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18, operative from 1989.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.64
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.64
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the flexibility of the Constitution:

1. A simple majority is counted against the full strength of the House, not against those present and voting.
2. Provisions amendable by a simple majority are amended under the procedure laid down in Article 368.
3. A change in the salaries and privileges of the Members of Parliament needs a special majority.
4. The simple-majority route keeps the Constitution responsive to day-to-day administrative and political needs.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it means more than half of the members present and voting. Statement 2 is incorrect: these provisions lie outside the scope of Article 368. Statement 3 is incorrect: this is a simple-majority subject. Statement 4 is correct: stated as the purpose of flexibility.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the matters that Parliament can change by a simple majority:

1. The quorum in Parliament.
2. The creation or abolition of legislative councils in the States needs ratification by half of the States.
3. The provisions relating to the official language.
4. The delimitation of constituencies.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: quorum is a simple-majority subject. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is a simple-majority subject, with no ratification. Statement 3 is correct: the official language provisions can be changed by a simple majority. Statement 4 is correct: delimitation is a simple-majority subject. So 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution, with the help of Laxmikanth:

1. The right to property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300-A.
2. The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
3. The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 reduced the Fundamental Duties from eleven to ten.
4. During a National Emergency even the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.66. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.66. Statement 3 is incorrect: it added one more duty, making eleven. Statement 4 is incorrect: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.66: the Fundamental Rights can be suspended except those under Articles 20 and 21. So 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. An amendment affecting the extent of the executive power of the Union and the States needs ratification by half of the States.
2. The formation of new States needs a special majority under Article 368.
3. A person who is not a Member of Parliament cannot be appointed a Union Minister.
4. The Prime Minister can dissolve the Lok Sabha without involving the President.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: extent of executive power needs ratification. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is a simple-majority subject outside Article 368. Statement 3 is incorrect: he may be appointed and must become a member within six months. Statement 4 is incorrect: the President dissolves it on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM. So 1 are correct (statements 1).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: No State in India has a constitutional right to secede from the Union.
Statement-II: Article 1 describes India as a Union of States, and the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the States.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: no State can secede. Statement-II is correct: and explains it: because the federation is not the product of an agreement among States, no State can claim the right to withdraw (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.64).
w: Rejected: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is also correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is also correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Crucial provisions of the Constitution cannot be changed casually.
Statement-II: Any amendment passed by a special majority becomes effective only after ratification by half of the States.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: crucial provisions need a special majority under Article 368. Statement-II is incorrect: only the federal-structure matters need ratification by half of the States; others become effective on the President's assent after the special majority.
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect.
Rejected: it is Statement-II that is incorrect, and Statement-I is the correct one.

questions.q:
Match each feature in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I
A. Dual executive
B. Collective responsibility
C. Single citizenship
D. Integrated judiciary

List-II
1. Council of Ministers answerable to the Lok Sabha and bound to resign on losing its majority
2. No separate State citizenship, in contrast to the USA
3. President as nominal head and Prime Minister with Council as real executive
4. Supreme Court, High Courts and subordinate courts forming a single hierarchy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Dual executive = nominal President and real PM-led Council; collective responsibility = Council answerable to the Lok Sabha; single citizenship = no State citizenship; integrated judiciary = one hierarchy of courts.
w: A and B are interchanged: Dual executive goes with President as nominal head and Prime Minister with Council as real executive, and Collective responsibility with Council of Ministers answerable to the Lok Sabha and bound to resign on losing its majority.

C and D are interchanged: Single citizenship goes with No separate State citizenship, in contrast to the USA, and Integrated judiciary with Supreme Court, High Courts and subordinate courts forming a single hierarchy.

B and C are interchanged: Collective responsibility goes with Council of Ministers answerable to the Lok Sabha and bound to resign on losing its majority, and Single citizenship with No separate State citizenship, in contrast to the USA.

concepts.name: Emergency provisions, Parts and Schedules
concepts.description: The three Emergencies and their Articles, the 22 original Parts and the later additions, and the twelve Schedules with their subjects and counts.
concepts.idea: Each Part and Schedule has a subject and an Article range that can be recalled with its amending Act.
concepts.rule: National Emergency is under Article 352, State Emergency under Articles 356 and 365, Financial Emergency under Article 360, all in Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360). Parts IV-A and XIV-A came with the 42nd Amendment, IX with the 73rd, IX-A with the 74th and IX-B with the 97th; Part VII was repealed by the 7th Amendment. The Schedules run from the First (States and Union Territories) to the Twelfth (Municipalities, 18 matters); the Eighth now has 22 languages, the Ninth came with the First Amendment, the Tenth with the 52nd, the Eleventh (29 matters) and Twelfth with the 73rd and 74th. According to Laxmikanth the Union List has 98, the State List 59 and the Concurrent List 52 subjects.
concepts.example: A Presidential Proclamation because of a threat to the credit of India is a Financial Emergency under Article 360, which lies in Part XVIII.

questions.q: A Proclamation by the President on the ground of a threat to the financial stability or credit of India falls under which one of the following Articles?
questions.e: Financial Emergency is under Article 360; National Emergency is Article 352; State Emergency (President's Rule) is Articles 356 and 365 (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.69).
w: Article 352 is the National Emergency, on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
Article 356 is President's Rule, on the ground of failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
Article 365 deals with failure to comply with directions of the Union and is linked to State Emergency.

questions.q: Part IX-B of the Constitution was inserted by an amendment of 2011. Which one of the following correctly pairs that amendment with the subject of the Part?
questions.e: Part IX-B, Articles 243ZH to 243ZT, on Co-operative Societies was added by the 97th Amendment (2011) (Laxmikanth ch.4 pp.69-70). Note that the Supreme Court in 2021 held this Part invalid in its application to State co-operative societies, for want of ratification by half the States.
w: The 73rd Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX on Panchayats.
The 74th Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX-A on Municipalities.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part XIV-A on Tribunals and is not an amendment of 2011.

questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992, lists the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats. How many matters does it contain?
questions.e: The Eleventh Schedule has 29 matters (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.81) and the Twelfth has 18.
w: 18 is the number of matters in the Twelfth Schedule, which belongs to Municipalities.
Close, but the Eleventh Schedule has 29 matters.
Not the figure given; the Eleventh Schedule has 29 matters.

questions.q: Which one of the following Amendment Acts added Sindhi to the languages of the Eighth Schedule?
questions.e: Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967); the 71st and 92nd added the others, and the 96th renamed Oriya (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.81).
w: The 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.
The 92nd added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.
The 96th only renamed Oriya as Odia.

questions.q: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule were originally shielded from judicial review on the ground of violation of Fundamental Rights. The Supreme Court later ruled that laws placed in it after a particular date are open to review. Which one of the following is that date?
questions.a: 24 April 1973, when Kesavananda Bharati was decided
o: 24 April 1973, when Kesavananda Bharati was decided
18 June 1951, the date of the First Amendment
26 January 1950, the commencement of the Constitution
25 June 1975, the day the Internal Emergency was declared
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Amendment (1951); laws included after 24 April 1973, when Kesavananda Bharati was decided, are open to judicial review (Supreme Court 2007; Laxmikanth ch.4 p.81).
w: That is when the Ninth Schedule was added, not the cut-off for review.
The Schedule did not exist at commencement; the cut-off is later.
The cut-off is the Kesavananda date, 1973, not the Emergency.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the emergency provisions of the Constitution:

1. National Emergency is provided for in Article 356.
2. State Emergency (President's Rule) is provided for in Articles 356 and 365.
3. Financial Emergency is provided for in Article 360.
4. The Emergency Provisions occupy Part XVIII, from Article 352 to Article 360.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 352 is National Emergency; 356 is President's Rule. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is correct: the whole Part runs 352 to 360.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Parts of the Constitution:

1. The Union and its Territory is the subject of Part I, which opens with Article 1 and closes at Article 4.
2. Part II, on Citizenship, covers Articles 5 to 12.
3. The Fundamental Rights of Part III lie in Articles 12 to 35.
4. Part IV (Directive Principles, Articles 36 to 51) is followed by Part V, on the Union, covering Articles 52 to 151.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as in the table. Statement 2 is incorrect: Part II ends at Article 11; Article 12 begins Part III. Statement 3 is correct: as in the table. Statement 4 is correct: Part V runs Articles 52 to 151, including the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Parts IV-A to VIII:

1. Part IV-A, consisting of the single Article 51A on Fundamental Duties, was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
2. Part VI, on the States, covers Articles 152 to 237.
3. Part VII, which dealt with the States in Part B of the First Schedule, was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956).
4. Part VIII, on the Union Territories, covers Articles 239 to 242.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as in the table. Statement 2 is correct: as in the table. Statement 3 is correct: it now covers no Articles. Statement 4 is correct: as in the table.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the local-government and tribal-area Parts:

1. Part IX deals with Panchayats, was added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), and covers Articles 243 to 243O.
2. Part IX-A deals with Municipalities, covers Articles 243P to 243ZG, and was added by the 74th Amendment (1992).
3. The 74th Amendment (1992) is the source of Part IX-B on Co-operative Societies.
4. Part X deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas and covers Articles 244 to 244A.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as in the table. Statement 2 is correct: as in the table. Statement 3 is incorrect: it was added by the 97th Amendment (2011). Statement 4 is correct: as in the table.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Parts XI to XIV-A:

1. Articles 245 to 263 form Part XI, which governs legislative and administrative relations between the Union and the States.
2. Part XII, on Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits, covers Articles 264 to 300A.
3. Part XIII, on Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within India, covers Articles 301 to 310.
4. Part XIV-A, on Tribunals, covering Articles 323A and 323B, was added by the 44th Amendment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: legislative and administrative relations. Statement 2 is correct: as in the table. Statement 3 is incorrect: it covers Articles 301 to 307; Part XIV begins at 308. Statement 4 is incorrect: it was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Parts XIV to XIX:

1. Part XIV, on Services under the Union and the States, covers Articles 308 to 329.
2. Part XV is headed Elections and spans Articles 324 to 329A.
3. Official Language forms Part XVII, running from Article 343 to Article 360.
4. Articles 361 to 367 are grouped in Part XIX, Miscellaneous.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it covers Articles 308 to 323; Part XIV-A and Part XV follow. Statement 2 is correct: as in the table. Statement 3 is incorrect: it covers Articles 343 to 351; Part XVIII begins at 352. Statement 4 is correct: as in the table.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the later Parts of the Constitution:

1. Under Part XVI, the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies was ended by the 104th Amendment, effective from January 2020.
2. Part XX, on the Amendment of the Constitution, covers Articles 368 to 370.
3. Articles 369 to 392 make up Part XXI, headed Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions.
4. Part XXII, on short title, commencement, authoritative text in Hindi and repeals, covers Articles 393 to 400.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the 104th Amendment ended the Anglo-Indian nominations from January 2020. Statement 2 is incorrect: Part XX consists of Article 368 alone; Part XXI starts at 369. Statement 3 is correct: as in the table. Statement 4 is incorrect: it covers Articles 393 to 395, the last Article being 395.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the First to Fourth Schedules:

1. The First Schedule contains the list of languages recognised by the Constitution.
2. The Second Schedule deals with the emoluments, allowances and privileges of the President, Governors, Speakers, Judges and the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
3. The Third Schedule prescribes the forms of oaths or affirmations for Union and State ministers, Members of Parliament and of State legislatures, Judges and the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
4. The Fourth Schedule allocates the seats of the Lok Sabha among the States.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it lists the States and Union Territories and their territorial jurisdiction; languages are in the Eighth Schedule. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is incorrect: it allocates Rajya Sabha seats to the States and Union Territories.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Schedules of the Constitution:

1. The Fifth Schedule contains provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
2. The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers between the Union and the States in the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
3. According to Laxmikanth, the Concurrent List presently contains 52 subjects.
4. Autonomous administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur and Mizoram is the subject of the Sixth Schedule.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as listed. Statement 2 is correct: three Lists. Statement 3 is correct: originally 47. Statement 4 is incorrect: the four States are Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Seventh and Eighth Schedules, according to Laxmikanth:

1. The Union List has gained one subject since the Constitution began, and now stands at 98.
2. The Concurrent List has shrunk from 52 subjects at the start to 47 now.
3. The State List presently contains 59 subjects, against 66 originally.
4. The Eighth Schedule originally listed 14 languages and presently lists 22.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as stated in Table 4.3. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was 47 originally and is 52 now. Statement 3 is correct: as stated in Table 4.3. Statement 4 is correct: as stated. So 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 3, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about additions to the Eighth Schedule:

1. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment of 1967.
2. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 92nd Amendment.
3. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 71st Amendment.
4. The 96th Amendment of 2011 renamed Oriya as Odia without adding a language.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as stated. Statement 2 is incorrect: they were added by the 71st Amendment (1992). Statement 3 is incorrect: they were added by the 92nd Amendment (2003). Statement 4 is correct: as stated in Laxmikanth. So 2 are correct (statements 1, 4).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 4).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 4).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ninth to Twelfth Schedules:

1. The Ninth Schedule was added by the 44th Amendment of 1978.
2. The Tenth Schedule, containing the anti-defection provisions, was added by the 42nd Amendment of 1976.
3. The Eleventh Schedule lists 18 matters relating to Panchayats.
4. The Twelfth Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment of 1992, lists 18 matters relating to Municipalities.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the First Amendment (1951) added it. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was added by the 52nd Amendment (1985). Statement 3 is incorrect: it lists 29 matters. Statement 4 is correct: as stated. So 1 are correct (statements 4).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Part VII of the Constitution at present covers no operative Articles.
Statement-II: Part XXII of the Constitution covers Articles 393 to 395, dealing with the short title, commencement, authoritative Hindi text and repeals.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Part VII, on the Part B States, was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956) and covers no Articles (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.75). Statement-II is correct: Part XXII covers Articles 393-395. The two concern different Parts, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Statement-II describes a different Part and says nothing about why Part VII is empty, so it does not explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct: Part XXII covers Articles 393 to 395.
Statement-I is correct: Part VII has no Articles after its repeal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 inserted the Part on Tribunals, numbered XIV-A.
Statement-II: The same 1976 Amendment inserted Part IV-A with the Fundamental Duties.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: and. Statement-II is correct: ; both Parts came with the same 1976 Amendment, but the addition of Fundamental Duties is no reason for the addition of Tribunals (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.75).
w: Rejected: Statement-II is true but it is not the reason for Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is also correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is also correct.

questions.q:
Pair each Schedule in List-I with what it deals with in List-II.

List-I
A. Second Schedule
B. Third Schedule
C. Fourth Schedule
D. Fifth Schedule

List-II
1. Seats in the Rajya Sabha for the States and Union Territories
2. Control and governance of Scheduled Areas together with the Scheduled Tribes
3. Salaries, allowances and privileges of office-holders such as the Governors and Judges
4. Forms of oaths or affirmations to be taken by ministers, legislators and Judges

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Second = emoluments and privileges of office-holders; Third = forms of oaths; Fourth = Rajya Sabha seats; Fifth = Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
w: A and B are interchanged: Second Schedule goes with Salaries, allowances and privileges of office-holders such as the Governors and Judges, and Third Schedule with Forms of oaths or affirmations to be taken by ministers, legislators and Judges.

C and D are interchanged: Fourth Schedule goes with Seats in the Rajya Sabha for the States and Union Territories, and Fifth Schedule with Control and governance of Scheduled Areas together with the Scheduled Tribes.

B and C are interchanged: Third Schedule goes with Forms of oaths or affirmations to be taken by ministers, legislators and Judges, and Fourth Schedule with Seats in the Rajya Sabha for the States and Union Territories.

concepts.name: Sources of the Constitution and federal-unitary mix
concepts.description: Which feature came from which country (Britain, USA, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Germany, South Africa, USSR, Japan, the 1935 Act) and the unitary features of a federal Constitution.
concepts.idea: A feature is matched to its source constitution and the 1935 Act supplies the structure.
concepts.rule: Britain gave parliamentary government, Rule of Law, single citizenship and prerogative writs; the USA gave Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of the judiciary and impeachment of the President; Ireland gave the Directive Principles, the method of electing the President and nomination to the Rajya Sabha; Canada a federation with a strong Centre and residuary powers with the Centre; Australia the Concurrent List, freedom of trade and the joint sitting; Weimar Germany the suspension of Fundamental Rights in Emergency; South Africa the amendment procedure; the USSR the Fundamental Duties. According to Laxmikanth the Federal Scheme, the office of Governor, Emergency provisions and advisory jurisdiction come from the Government of India Act, 1935. The Constitution is federal in form and unitary in spirit.
concepts.example: The nomination of twelve members to the Rajya Sabha follows the Irish model, while their election follows South Africa according to Laxmikanth.

questions.q: The practice of nominating members to the Rajya Sabha has been drawn from the Constitution of which one of the following countries?
questions.e: Ireland supplied the Directive Principles, the method of electing the President and nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.82, Table 4.4).
w: South Africa is credited with the procedure for election of Rajya Sabha members, not with nomination.
Canada is credited with a strong-Centre federation and residuary powers, not Rajya Sabha nomination.
Australia is credited with the Concurrent List, freedom of trade and the joint sitting.

questions.q: The provision that Fundamental Rights may be suspended during an Emergency is traced to which one of the following sources?
questions.e: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency is borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany; the Emergency provisions as a whole come from the Government of India Act, 1935 (Laxmikanth ch.4 pp.63, 82).
w: The 1935 Act supplied the Emergency powers generally, but it had no Fundamental Rights to suspend; the suspension of rights is credited to Weimar.
The Soviet Constitution is credited with Fundamental Duties and the ideal of justice.
Canada is credited with a strong-Centre federation and residuary powers.

questions.q: The procedure for amendment of the Constitution of India is credited to which one of the following Constitutions?
questions.e: The amendment procedure is credited to the South African Constitution (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.82, which also credits it with the election of Rajya Sabha members).
w: Ireland is credited with DPSP, election of the President and nomination to the Rajya Sabha.
The British Constitution is flexible and has no special amending procedure; it supplied parliamentary government.
The Soviet Constitution is credited with Fundamental Duties and the ideal of justice.

questions.q: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse within the country, found in Part XIII of the Constitution, is credited to the Constitution of which one of the following?
questions.e: Australia gave the Concurrent List, freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, and the joint sitting of the two Houses (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.82). Part XIII covers Articles 301 to 307.
w: Ireland is credited with DPSP and the method of electing the President.
Japan is credited with the procedure established by law.
The USSR is credited with Fundamental Duties and the ideal of justice.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens in Part IV-A were inspired by which one of the following Constitutions?
questions.e: Fundamental Duties are credited to the USSR Constitution (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.82); they were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
w: Ireland inspired the Directive Principles, not the duties.
Japan is credited with the procedure established by law.
France is credited with the republic and liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about features borrowed from the British Constitution:

1. The American Constitution is the source of India's single citizenship.
2. The parliamentary form of government was borrowed from Britain.
3. The Rule of Law was borrowed from Britain.
4. Prerogative writs were borrowed from Britain.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the chapter credits single citizenship to the British Constitution; the USA has dual citizenship. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is correct: as listed.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about features borrowed from the American Constitution:

1. Fundamental Rights were borrowed from the American Constitution.
2. Judicial review was borrowed from the American Constitution.
3. The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the American Constitution.
4. Impeachment of the President was modelled on the procedure in the US Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as listed. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is incorrect: they come from the Irish Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: as listed.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about features credited to the Irish and South African Constitutions:

1. The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from Ireland.
2. South Africa is the source of the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.
3. The method of election of the President was borrowed from Ireland.
4. According to Laxmikanth, the election of the members of the Rajya Sabha was borrowed from South Africa.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as listed. Statement 2 is incorrect: Ireland is the source; South Africa is credited with the election of Rajya Sabha members. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is correct: Table 4.4 (ch.4 p.82).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about features credited to the Canadian Constitution, according to Laxmikanth:

1. A federation with a strong Centre was borrowed from Canada.
2. Canada is where the idea of vesting residuary powers in the Centre comes from.
3. The appointment of State governors by the Centre was borrowed from Canada.
4. The Canadian Constitution is the source of the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.4. Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.4. Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.4. Statement 4 is incorrect: the joint sitting is credited to Australia.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following features which, according to Laxmikanth, are drawn from the Government of India Act, 1935:

1. The Federal Scheme.
2. The office of Governor.
3. The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
4. The Emergency provisions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: listed against the 1935 Act. Statement 2 is correct: listed against the 1935 Act. Statement 3 is correct: listed against the 1935 Act. Statement 4 is correct: listed against the 1935 Act; the suspension of Fundamental Rights, however, is credited to Weimar.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about borrowed features:

1. The USSR Constitution supplied the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.
2. Australia is the country from which the Concurrent List was taken.
3. The phrase 'procedure established by law' traces to the Japanese Constitution.
4. The Soviet Constitution is where the Preamble's liberty, equality and fraternity come from.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it is credited to Australia. Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.4. Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.4 (ch.4 p.82). Statement 4 is incorrect: they come from the French Constitution.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.82
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.82
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sources of the Constitution:

1. The idea of Fundamental Duties for citizens traces to the Soviet Constitution.
2. Weimar Germany is the source of the provision allowing Fundamental Rights to be suspended in an Emergency.
3. The amendment procedure was borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany.
4. Prerogative writs were borrowed from the American Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as listed. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is credited to South Africa. Statement 4 is incorrect: they are credited to the British Constitution.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements from the summary of borrowings and features:

1. Cabinet government comes from Britain, Fundamental Rights from the USA and the Directive Principles from Ireland.
2. The Concurrent List and the Emergency provisions were both borrowed from the Weimar Constitution.
3. A single Constitution for the Centre and the States is a federal feature of the Constitution.
4. Single citizenship and the all-India services are among the unitary features of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: these are the standard borrowings. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Concurrent List is from Australia and the Emergency provisions from the 1935 Act, with only the suspension of Fundamental Rights from Weimar. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is among the unitary features. Statement 4 is correct: as listed.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Fundamental Rights were borrowed from Ireland and the Directive Principles from the USA.
2. The Soviet Constitution is the source of impeachment of the President.
3. The independence of the judiciary and judicial review were borrowed from the American Constitution.
4. The Weimar Constitution is the source of the method of electing the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the sources are the other way round. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is credited to the American Constitution. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is incorrect: the method of election of the President is credited to the Irish Constitution.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about borrowed features:

1. The independence of the judiciary was borrowed from the American Constitution.
2. Single citizenship was borrowed from the British Constitution.
3. The Rule of Law was borrowed from the American Constitution.
4. The parliamentary form of government was borrowed from the American Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: as listed. Statement 2 is correct: as listed. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is British. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is British; the USA has a presidential system. So 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements, with the help of Laxmikanth:

1. At adoption the Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules, and at present it has about 470 Articles in 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.
2. According to Laxmikanth, the Government of India Act, 1935 is the most profound influence and material source of the Constitution.
3. Both the judiciary and the Public Service Commissions are, in Laxmikanth's account, inherited from the 1935 Act.
4. The philosophical part of the Constitution, the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles, is derived from the Government of India Act, 1935.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.62. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.63. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch.4 p.63. Statement 4 is incorrect: its inspiration comes from the American and Irish Constitutions; the structural part comes from the 1935 Act. So 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the unitary and federal features:

1. A single Constitution for the Centre and the States is a federal feature.
2. A dual polity is a unitary feature of the Constitution.
3. An integrated judiciary is a unitary feature of the Constitution.
4. An independent judiciary is a unitary feature of the Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it is a unitary feature. Statement 2 is incorrect: dual polity is the federal form. Statement 3 is correct: as listed. Statement 4 is incorrect: Laxmikanth lists the independent judiciary among the federal features. So 1 are correct (statements 3).
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 3).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Indian Constitution is described as federal in form but unitary in spirit.
Statement-II: The Constitution provides for a single citizenship, a single Constitution for the Centre and the States, an integrated judiciary, all-India services and emergency provisions.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The Indian Constitution is described as federal in form but unitary in spirit. Statement-II is correct: and explains it: the listed features concentrate power at the Centre and so give the federal form a unitary spirit (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.64).
w: Rejected: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is also correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is also correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Indian Constitution is a blend of rigidity and flexibility.
Statement-II: Amendments to the Indian Constitution follow the same procedure as ordinary laws.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Article 368 special majority gives rigidity and the simple-majority route gives flexibility. Statement-II is incorrect: only some provisions can be amended like ordinary laws; crucial ones need the special majority (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.63).
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect.
Rejected: it is Statement-II that is incorrect, and Statement-I is the correct one.

questions.q:
Match each source country in List-I with a feature borrowed from it, in List-II.

List-I
A. Ireland
B. Australia
C. Japan
D. Canada

List-II
1. Concurrent List
2. Residuary powers vested in the Centre
3. Method of election of the President
4. Procedure established by law

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Ireland - method of election of the President; Australia - Concurrent List; Japan - procedure established by law; Canada - residuary powers with the Centre (Laxmikanth ch.4 p.82).
w: A and B are interchanged: Ireland goes with Method of election of the President, and Australia with Concurrent List.
C and D are interchanged: Japan goes with Procedure established by law, and Canada with Residuary powers vested in the Centre.
B and C are interchanged: Australia goes with Concurrent List, and Japan with Procedure established by law.
